children: , the enterprise-software and infrastructure provider, added LTM as a deployment partner for Lightwell on Wednesday. IBM shares slipped approximately 0.2% to $231.48, suggesting investors remain unconvinced that another distribution channel will quickly turn the AI-powered security platform into meaningful revenue.

IBM committed $5 billion earlier this year to Lightwell and related open-source security initiatives. The platform deploys AI agents to find vulnerabilities, build patches and test the fixes, generating 7,500 patches during its first two weeks. LTM will bring integration, validation and DevSecOps support to enterprise customers. That matters because clever technology is only the starting line; dependable deployment is what gets corporate budgets moving.

IBM ended the second quarter with $8.2 billion in cash and $62 billion in debt, so the program's $5 billion headline commitment equals roughly 61% of its cash balance, although the spending will unfold over time. Quarterly software revenue increased 5% to $7.8 billion, while infrastructure revenue declined 7%. The picture adds a modest valuation cushion: IBM's $231.48 share price stands 4.56% below its GF Value estimate of $242.54. Lightwell now needs to convert that promise into recurring software growth as the legacy infrastructure business loses ground.

title: IBM Slips as Its $5 Billion AI Security Bet Finds a Builder
